figures.label: fig:quotient-layers
figures.planned_location: Section 3, after the full-versus-symplectic quotient comparison and before the local pseudo-symmetry-cost discussion
source_fields: proof markers: cyclic-vector torsor, quotient identity, and outside-scope boundary
figures.transformation: Compose the full shell-to-cyclic-locus inclusion, torsor identification, cyclic A-orbit layer, full and symplectic quotient cards, and a retention ledger. The reversor row records both d-to-minus-d pairing and the absence of cyclic/noncyclic mixing. Only q=5 and q=11 enter as displayed numerical discard controls.
figures.caption_claim: The cyclic locus is a full-centralizer torsor; the full residual quotient has one class, the symplectic quotient retains norm-image classes, and both coarse induced A maps are identity.
limitations: All-q authority is the proof package, not the two displayed discard controls.
The reversor may merge the split noncyclic d and minus-d strata, but it does not mix the noncyclic complement with the cyclic locus.
Burnside, orbifold, stacky, groupoid, and twisted-sector refinements are outside scope, not ruled out.

figures.label: fig:nine-modulus-ledger
figures.planned_location: Section 5, immediately after introducing the registered nine-modulus audit and before the compact manuscript ledger table
figures.transformation: Plot exact integers in the registered source order as two count panels and one fully annotated quotient ledger; encode unaudited composite reversor cells as n/a.
figures.caption_claim: At every frozen control the cyclic locus has full-centralizer cardinality and one full cyclic quotient class, while the symplectic quotient retains the exact norm-image count and the full shell may retain noncyclic strata.
limitations: All nine moduli were development-seen fixed controls.
The ledger neither fits a trend nor proves any all-q formula.
Composite reversing groups were not audited and are not encoded as zero.

figures.label: fig:clock-semantics
figures.planned_location: Section 6, after the abstract identity-factor statement and before the Route-A disposition
source_fields: proof markers: quotient primitive period one and outside-scope boundary
figures.transformation: Contrast exact source orders with native coarse quotient period one; diagram the intrinsic formal factor separately from an external symbolic q label; compare the fixed prime and composite class cards.
figures.caption_claim: The source A clock is erased by both coarse centralizer quotients, q-indexing is externally supplied, and composites pass the same one-class construction, so the coarse mechanism has no intrinsic prime selector.
limitations: The expressions q^(-s) and log q are symbolic and are not evaluated.
The figure addresses only the coarse quotient.
Equivariant, orbifold, stacky, groupoid, twisted-sector, transfer, quantum, and Hecke constructions remain untested.
